tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

zapata-purpose-and-audience: Chapter 1, p.5: the author states the book's purpose and intended readers in his own words.
zapata-self-described-as-introductory-no: Chapter 1, p.5 and footnote 1: the author states the Chapter 2 depth and that the basics are in his earlier notes (QC1, QC2); Chapter 1 also says technical detail is kept light.
zapata-decoherence-definition: Section 2.2, p.12: the author names the destruction of quantum behavior by environment interaction 'decoherence' in the passage that introduces the term.
zapata-nisq-era-definition: Section 2.3, p.14: the author introduces and characterizes the NISQ era (moderate noise, few qubits and gates). The 'currently in' clause is context, not what the grade rests on.
zapata-hybrid-algorithms-definition: Section 2.3, p.14: the author introduces the term hybrid quantum-classical algorithms and says what the two parts do.
zapata-portfolio-objective-min-risk-give: Section 3.1.1, p.20, Eqs 3.1.17-3.1.19: the author states the problem he uses (minimize risk for return M, weights sum to one) and defines the risk aversion coefficient.
zapata-greeks-delta-gamma-theta-definiti: Section 3.2.2, pp.24-26: delta (Eq 3.2.15), gamma (derivative of delta, from the 'acceleration' passage) and theta (Eq 3.2.23) are defined by the author and used in the Black-Scholes form Eq 3.2.24.
zapata-ml-definition-and-scope: Section 3.3, p.27: the author states what ML is for this guide (algorithms that learn from data without further programming; goal is patterns for predictions or decisions).
zapata-qml-data-encoding-methods: Section 4.2.1, pp.52-55: the author defines basis, amplitude (with normalization and 2^Q >= I padding) and angle encoding by explicit maps. The value matches those maps.
zhang19-indirect-pump-approach: Abstract and Section 1, p.1: the authors state their own method, modulating only the pump; Sections 3 and 4 run it.
zhang19-extinction-definition: Section 2, p.3: the paper defines conversion extinction as the ratio of fiber-coupled SF power of two modes under the same pump.
zhang19-diffraction-regime-sfg: Section 1, p.2: the authors state the regime (SFG in lithium niobate, strong diffraction) and the pump-shaping mechanism they use. Their measured performance is separate and not claimed by this value.
zhang19-numerical-model: Section 2, p.2: SVEA coupled equations (2)-(4) and the split-step Fourier, adaptive-step solver are stated as the paper's own simulation method.
zhang19-kolmogorov-turbulence-model: Section 2, Eq.(5), p.3: the paper states the Kolmogorov model and the spectrum 0.0033 c_n^2 k^(-11/3), valid for 1/L0 << k << 1/l0.
zhang19-strehl-ratio-definition: Section 2, Eq.(6), p.3: turbulence strength is defined through SR; SR = 0 is maximum turbulence and SR = 1 is none.
zhang19-laser-pulse-parameters: Section 3, p.2: the setup text states the wavelengths, 200 ps FWHM and 10 MHz rate.
zhang19-pump-signal-power: Section 3, p.2: the setup text states the pump and signal average and peak powers.
zhang19-beam-sizes-slm: Section 3, p.2: beam sizes, the Santec SLM-100 and the 50 and 55 degree angles are stated in the setup.
zhang19-ppln-crystal: Section 3, p.2: poling period, MgO doping and crystal size are stated in the setup.
zhang19-beam-waists-in-crystal: Section 3, p.2: the waists of 45 and 41 um are stated in the setup.
zhang19-sf-output-wavelength: Section 3, p.2: the SF center wavelength 775.85 nm and 0.05 nm FWHM are stated in the setup, as is Fig. 1.
zhang19-detection-and-feedback-loop: Section 3, p.3: the single-mode fiber, power meter and MATLAB feedback to the pump SLM are stated in the setup.
zhang19-turbulence-emulated-on-slm: Section 3, p.3: the paper states turbulence is emulated by adding phase noise to the signal SLM masks, so turbulence results cover emulated turbulence, not real propagation.
zhang19-pso-and-feedback-optimization: Section 4, pp.3-4: the paper states its optimization procedure (PSO, then adaptive feedback) and its own caveat that the measured selectivity is below simulation.
zhang19-table1-target-and-suppressed-mod: Section 4, Table 1 text, p.4: the paper states which target and suppressed modes the Table 1 experiment covers, and the xi_i definition.
zhang19-reoptimization-limit-higher-orde: Section 4, p.4: the authors state that re-optimization helps the higher-order LG modes less, and give their reason. A limit on their own method.
zhang19-deselection-definition-and-metho: Section 4, p.5: the paper defines deselection and the negative-extinction sign convention. The modification claim is demonstrated in Fig. 6.
zhang19-strong-turbulence-recovery-limit: Section 4, p.6: the authors state that recovery under strong turbulence is weaker and give their reason. A limit on their own method.
review-scope-circuit-model: Section 5, p.18: the authors state this is not a complete review and cover the circuit model only.
review-perspective-fundamentals-to-appli: Section 1, p.2: the authors state the review's perspective and its four-part organization (Sections 2 to 5).
entanglement-definition: Section 2.1, p.3, Eq.(5): the paper shows a two-qubit state that is not a tensor product and calls this case entanglement.
swap-test-purpose-and-outcome: Section 3.2, pp.7-8, Eqs 22-27: the paper derives P(0)=1/2+1/2|<a|b>|^2 step by step, so the overlap is read from the control-qubit probability. The value claims no more.

theory_low.zapata-bit-flip-repetition-code-example: Section 2.2, pp.12-13: an illustrative example, argued informally, with the parity check referred to QC1; nothing is proved here.
theory_low.zapata-binary-portfolio-optimization-is-: Section 3.1.1, pp.19-20, Eqs 3.1.20-3.1.25: an informal term matching, with the Lagrange multiplier treated as a free linear coefficient and no proof of equivalence. The value also adds that QUBO is NP-hard, which the paper only states as known, not proved.
theory_low.zapata-vqe-hybrid-structure: Section 4.1.1, pp.46-47: a description of a known algorithm, referred to QC2; the upper-bound relation is stated, not proved here.
theory_low.zapata-portfolio-cost-hamiltonian-constr: Section 4.1.1, pp.47-48: the equivalence is asserted ('the variational quantum method establishes') and the Pauli rewriting is shown without a proof or a check.
theory_low.zapata-qaoa-structure-and-layers: Section 4.1.2, pp.49-52: a description of a known algorithm; the claim that more layers give better approximation is cited, not proved.
theory_low.zapata-qnn-architecture-description: Section 4.2.1, p.56: a schematic description of a generic QNN under 'suppose' assumptions; the parameter count is a rough 'at most' bound. No result.
theory_low.grover-amplitude-amplification-mechanism: Section 3.1, p.6: an informal motivation ('a spontaneous thought'), not a proof; the correctness and iteration count are cited.
theory_low.phase-estimation-core-of-hhl: Section 3.3, pp.8-9: the claim that phase estimation is core to HHL-like algorithms is a field statement; the target statement is an informal framing, with no proof here.
